text:
Maya: Heads up — we saw a tail latency regression on Dedicated cluster last night. +28% p99 for MoE models, looks correlated with token routing spikes.
Arjun: Where in the stack? routing, NCCL, or kernel execution?
Maya: Initial flamegraphs point to a big bump inside the routing phase — all-to-all step and post-shuffle kernel stalls.
Sasha: Any link to the trace?
Maya: https://internal/trace/1951123456 — skim: spikes at 'expert_shuffle' and then a long idle inside 'dispatch_kernel'
Kevin: Uploading the short cpu/gpu trace we grabbed.
ProfilingBot: Attached files: gpu_timeline.pb, nvtx_trace.json, pprof_cpu.pb
Jules: Quick glance: NCCL all-to-all durations are fine but there are gaps between submit->wait on the compute stream. Looks like comm/compute not overlapped.
Arjun: Could be single-stream enqueue ordering. Are we launching copy/comm on the same stream as kernels?
Sasha: The runtime normally uses stream 0 for kernels and stream 1 for comm. But the MoE path has a micro-optimizer that collapses streams for small batches — maybe regressed there.
Maya: I reproduced locally with smaller config: when batching hits the new "adaptive_prefix_batcher" we see routing fanout increase (more tokens per minibatch) and a skew in expert assignment leading to hotspotting.
Kevin: Paste of shortened nvprof window:
```
# nvprof capture
Time(ms)  Kernel/Activity            Duration(ms)
0.0       routing_alltoall            12.4
12.4      dispatch_kernel             18.7  <-- many small kernels back-to-back
31.1      sparse_expert_mul           0.9
32.0      idle                        45.0  <-- wait for pending NCCL
77.0      finalize                    3.2
```
Sasha: Ouch — there is a 45ms idle between compute chunks. That explains tail. If NCCL kickoff is delayed, kernels sit idle.
Arjun: What's causing NCCL delay? We saw NCCL launch times increase in the new kernel selector change: fallback to the generic allreduce path for some expert sizes, meaning more host coordination.
Jules: Also worth noting: KV cache prefetch/eviction in the new prefix-cache changes ordering of tokens, which can increase cross-GPU expert fanout. I saw routing tables with higher entropy.
Maya: TL;DR: two coupled regressions: the adaptive batcher increases token fanout, and the kernel-selector change introduced additional host-side syncs that prevented comm/compute overlap.
Kevin: Quick experiment idea: force the old kernel selector for MoE dispatch only and run the internal perf harness with synthetic routing patterns.
Sasha: Agreed. Also add a micro-benchmark that stresses skewed expert distribution (50% tokens -> single expert) to capture extreme tail.
Arjun: For immediate mitigation we can: 1) temporarily revert the kernel-selector patch for MoE dispatch, 2) limit adaptive_prefix_batcher max_fanout threshold, 3) bump comm to dedicated stream and ensure cudaEvent-based sync rather than host sync.
Maya: Created ticket RW-PRF-3215 with repro script and artifacts. Assigning: Arjun (kernel selector revert), Sasha (batcher param), Jules (nvprof cross-check + perf harness).
ProfilingBot: Perf test scheduled: ci/perf/moe_fanout/skewed/1951123456 (runs nightly)
OpsBot: Deployed a canary that caps batcher fanout at 128 on dedicated-prod-2 as a heat shield. Monitoring p99.
Jules: One more note — kernel internals: the fused dispatch+softmax kernel we use for experts is sensitive to warps-per-expert. If batching increases token count per launch, it may pick a fallback path (less optimized) — check selector heuristics for token_count threshold.
Kevin: I'll add telemetry to log which kernel path is selected at runtime (short ID + reason) — should make root cause clearer.
Maya: Thanks. If we can get telemetry + the perf harness reproducing before EOD, we can ship the revert and the fanout cap together.
Arjun: Planning to open a PR that gates the new selector behind an opt-in flag for MoE until we validate overlap.
Sasha: And I'll add a unit test for the batcher to prevent future fanout regressions (assert peak_fanout <= 256 by default).
Maya: Great. Keep updates in this thread and paste perf diffs. :thumbsup:
